rules.title: Prohibition on Coordinated Pricing Algorithms to Set Rents or Manage Occupancy (BMC Ch. 13.63)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license, or provide to Berkeley landlords a coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential units in Berkeley, and unlawful for landlords to use one when setting rents or occupancy levels. Each month of violation and each affected unit is a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation (enforceable by City Attorney or aggrieved tenant)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley and to sellers/providers of algorithms to City of Berkeley landlords. 'Competitor Data' is nonpublic data on actual rents, occupancy, lease dates, etc. for other properties that is less than 90 days old.
rules.exemptions: Excludes (a) products that publish aggregated, anonymous rental data without recommending rents, fees, or occupancy; (b) products used to set rent or income limits under affordable housing guidelines; (c) products used for market research for project financing, appraisals, or research/testing/training for software development (so long as Competitor Data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated for a Berkeley landlord).
rules.interaction: Local ordinance only; it does not regulate the amount of rent a landlord may charge and does not restrict software that uses public data.
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code § 13.63.030 (Ch. 13.63, as amended by Ordinance No. 7,992-N.S.)
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley

rules.title: California application screening fee cap and conditions (Civ. Code § 1950.6)
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge an application screening fee only up to actual out-of-pocket costs plus the reasonable value of time spent, and never more than $30 per applicant (CPI-adjustable). No fee may be charged when no unit is or will soon be available. The landlord must offer either first-come-first-served screening or a refund to unselected applicants, and must give an itemized receipt and a copy of any credit report.
rules.key_value: $30 per applicant, adjustable annually for CPI increases beginning January 1, 1998
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to a landlord (an owner of residential rental property) or their agent charging an applicant (including a guarantor or cosignor) to rent a residential housing unit.
rules.exemptions: Not intended to preempt provisions or regulations governing deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs. A landlord may accept a reusable screening report under Section 1950.1. No refund is required for an applicant denied after consideration for failing established screening criteria. The fee is not treated as an 'advance fee' or as 'security'.
rules.interaction: Applies notwithstanding Section 1950.5 (security deposits); the fee is not considered 'security' under that section. Does not preempt federal or state housing assistance program rules on deposits and fees.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act statewide rent cap
rules.requirement: An owner of residential real property may not raise the gross rental rate by more than 5 percent plus the local percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period. No more than two increases are allowed in a 12-month period, and the owner must give notice of each increase under Civ. Code § 827.
rules.key_value: 5% + CPI change, max 10% (whichever is lower), over any 12-month period; max two increments per 12 months
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential real property (any dwelling or unit intended for human habitation, including units in a mobilehome park). It does not apply to a new tenancy's initial rent, when no prior tenant remains in lawful possession. Not covered: housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome). Applies to rent increases on or after March 15, 2019; for mobilehome tenancies, on or after February 18, 2021.
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; dormitories of higher education or K-12 schools; housing under a stricter local rent control ordinance that limits annual increases to less than the state cap; housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); separately alienable property whose owner is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, with the required written exemption notice; a duplex where the owner occupies one unit as principal residence (neither unit an ADU or JADU); homeowners of a mobilehome.
rules.interaction: Does not limit or expand local governments' authority to adopt rent control consistent with Civ. Code § 1954.50 et seq. Housing under a valid local rent control that restricts annual increases to less than the state cap is exempt, so stricter local rules govern. The state cap acts as a floor for covered units in jurisdictions without a stricter local rule.
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.

rules.title: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5 – Security deposit cap
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security (any deposit, fee or advance charge) above one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent. A narrower class of small landlords is capped at two months' rent, and the two-month cap does not apply if the prospective tenant is a service member.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (2 months' rent for qualifying small landlords)
rules.coverage_conditions: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling. The two-month cap applies only if the landlord is a natural person or an LLC whose members are all natural persons, and owns no more than two residential rental properties that collectively include no more than four dwelling units offered for rent.
rules.exemptions: Advance payment of not less than six months' rent is allowed if the lease term is six months or longer; mutually agreed paid alterations requested by the tenant; the cap does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024. Service members cannot be charged the 2-month small-landlord amount; higher-than-standard security for service members due to credit etc. must be explained in writing and the excess returned after no more than six months of residency if the tenant is not in arrears.
rules.interaction: Statewide rule; the document does not address local ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.

rules.title: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5 – Landlord photograph requirements
rules.requirement: For tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord must photograph the unit at or immediately before the start of the tenancy. Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord must also photograph the unit after possession is returned and after any repairs or cleanings, and provide those photographs with the itemized statement when deductions are made.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies where security is held; move-in photographs apply to tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025.
rules.interaction: Statewide rule; the document does not address local ordinances.

rules.title: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5 – Return of deposit and itemized statement within 21 days
rules.requirement: Within 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates, the landlord must furnish an itemized statement of the basis for and amount of any deductions and return any remaining security. Deductions are limited to amounts reasonably necessary for unpaid rent, damage beyond ordinary wear and tear, and cleaning to the move-in condition, and copies of invoices or receipts are required unless deductions total $125 or less or the tenant waived the right.
rules.key_value: 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential security for a rental agreement for property used as the tenant's dwelling.
rules.exemptions: Documentation requirements do not apply if deductions for repairs and cleaning together do not exceed $125 or the tenant validly waived them; good-faith estimates are allowed where repairs or documents cannot be completed within 21 days, with completion within 14 days.
rules.interaction: Statewide rule; the document does not address local ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated the premises, but not earlier than the time that either the landlord or the tenant provides a notice to terminate the tenancy under Section 1946 or 1946.1, Section 1161 of the Code of Civil Procedure, or not earlier than 60 calendar days prior to

rules.title: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5 – No 'nonrefundable' deposits
rules.requirement: A lease or rental agreement may not characterize any security as nonrefundable.
rules.coverage_conditions: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling.
rules.interaction: Statewide rule; the document does not address local ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: A lease or rental agreement shall not contain a provision characterizing any security as “nonrefundable.”

rules.title: Algorithmic rent fixing prohibited (Hoboken Code § 158-2)
rules.requirement: Landlords renting any residential dwelling unit in Hoboken may not fix prices using algorithmic pricing. That means using software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to collect and analyze nonpublic competitor information in order to coordinate, recommend or implement rents, lease terms or occupancy levels among competing lessors.
rules.key_value: Prohibition on algorithmic price fixing; penalties up to a $2,000 fine and/or up to 90 days community service, or as prescribed under N.J.S.A. 40:49-5
rules.coverage_conditions: Any residential dwelling unit, defined as any primary residence, in the City of Hoboken. 'Nonpublic competitor information' is information less than 365 days old that is not widely and readily available to the public at no cost.
rules.exemptions: Medical/long-term care and detention facilities are excluded from the definition of residential dwelling unit.
rules.interaction: Enforced by the Division of Housing or any aggrieved private citizen in Hoboken Municipal Court. The document does not discuss interaction with state law.
rules.quoted_span: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing.

rules.title: Mandatory disclosures for rent increases over 10% (Hoboken Code § 158-1)
rules.requirement: Residential landlords who raise rent by more than 10% year over year on renewal of a current tenant's lease must give the tenant specified disclosures before the increase takes effect. The disclosures are an itemization of costs, a statement on whether a rent algorithm was used, notice of the tenant's right to take legal action, and Division of Housing contact information. They go either on the first page of the renewal lease or on a Division of Housing form.
rules.key_value: Disclosure required for increases of more than 10% year over year; fine up to $1,000 per incident
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential landlords seeking to increase rent by more than 10% upon renewal of a lease with a current tenant, year over year.
rules.interaction: This is a disclosure requirement, not a cap on rent increases. It does not displace state law; the required notice itself refers to local or state law limits.

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO - legal grounds for eviction and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: RSO tenants may be evicted only for listed at-fault or no-fault reasons. No-fault evictions require a Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict filed with LAHD, 30-day and 60-day written notices, and payment of tenant relocation assistance. All termination notices must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service.
rules.key_value: No-fault evictions require relocation assistance. Notices filed with LAHD within 3 business days of service.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (generally first built on or before October 1, 1978). Properties not covered by the RSO are subject to the separate citywide Just Cause Ordinance.
rules.interaction: The page says non-RSO properties remain subject to the City's Just Cause Ordinance. State just cause law is not discussed.

rules.title: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance - annual allowable rent increase
rules.requirement: Landlords of RSO units may raise rent only once every 12 months, and only by the annual allowable rent increase percentage published by LAHD. Other increases require LAHD approval, for example capital improvement or just-and-reasonable programs.
rules.key_value: Once per 12 months, by the published allowable rent increase percentage (the percentage itself is not stated on this page). Utilities add-on removed and dependent 10% add-on removed effective 2026-02-02.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, plus replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28. Includes apartments, duplexes, ADUs/JADUs and similar units. Condominiums and townhomes are not rent-regulated for tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995.
rules.exemptions: Rent may be raised to market rate if the tenant voluntarily moves out, is evicted for nonpayment or lease violation, is evicted for failure to comply with a Tenant Habitability Plan, is evicted per a City Attorney order, or accepts a Tenant Buyout Agreement. Luxury exemption available by application.
rules.interaction: City rent control is stricter than, and operates alongside, state rent cap law. State law is not discussed in this document.
rules.quoted_span: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage

rules.title: Statewide prohibition on rent control (M.G.L. c. 40P, § 4)
rules.requirement: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind. A municipality that accepts chapter 40P may adopt only a limited regime that is voluntary for owners after six months, does not regulate occupancy, services, evictions, condominium conversion or removal from regulation, and compensates owners from general funds.
rules.key_value: General ban on rent control; narrow exception only for rent control that is voluntary for owners and funded by compensation to owners
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to every Massachusetts city and town. Exception rent control may not apply to any rental unit owned by a person or entity owning less than ten rental units, or to any unit with a fair market rent exceeding $400.
rules.exemptions: Exception for a city or town that accepts chapter 40P: compliance becomes entirely voluntary after six months from initial adoption, and the municipality must compensate owners for the difference between fair market rent and the below-market controlled rent from general funds.
rules.interaction: Preempts municipal rent control ordinances statewide, including in Boston and Cambridge. Local rent control or rent stabilization is effectively barred unless it meets the voluntary and compensated exception.

rules.title: Massachusetts 2026 rent control ballot initiative (struck by SJC)
rules.requirement: The proposed statewide initiative would have limited annual rent increases for residences, but the Supreme Judicial Court ruled it cannot go on the November 2026 ballot because its exemptions relate to religion.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residences generally; the article does not state the cap formula or unit thresholds.
rules.exemptions: Several types of units, including ones "operated solely for … religious … purposes."
rules.interaction: Would have created a statewide rent cap, but it is not law; Massachusetts currently has no statewide rent control. Supporters floated a compromise bill before July 1 that top lawmakers did not take up, and they hinted at a possible 2028 petition.
rules.citation: Mass. Const. amend. art. 48 (Initiative Petitions, The Initiative, II, § 2); Mass. SJC ruling on rent control ballot petition (June 2026)
rules.quoted_span: The proposal limits annual rent increases for residences, but it carved out exemptions for several types of units, including ones “operated solely for … religious … purposes."
rules.conflict_note: Proponents suggest the petition is "easily fixable" and may be refiled for the 2028 ballot; a compromise bill was floated but not passed as of the article. The article does not give the SJC case name or the proposed cap details. Secondary source (secondary (law firm / news / mirror)); confirm against the official text.

rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: It is unlawful, and a violation of the New Jersey Antitrust Act, for rental property owners to pay for or use a coordinator's services, for coordinators to facilitate agreements restricting competition, for persons to engage in or facilitate parallel pricing coordination, or for any person to perform a coordinating function (algorithmic setting or recommendation of rents, lease terms or occupancy using shared competitively sensitive information).
rules.key_value: Ban on algorithmic coordination of rental prices, material lease terms and occupancy levels
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental property owners (persons owning one or more rental residential dwelling units, including controlling-interest holders), coordinators (operators of algorithmic revenue management software or algorithmic devices performing a coordinating function) and any person; residential dwelling units are units intended as a primary residence in the State.
rules.exemptions: Excluded from 'coordinating function': research, statistical analysis or testing not used to set or recommend prices or terms; free public rent estimates; real estate brokerage databases available on equal terms that do not set or recommend prices; government entities setting or limiting rents through affordability controls. Residential dwelling unit excludes inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities. Spreadsheets without AI that require human analysis, and databases that only query unprocessed data, are not algorithmic devices.
rules.interaction: Section 6(b) prohibits a municipality from enacting an ordinance that conflicts with this act (except ordinances explicitly authorized or required by other law). The act supplements and does not limit the New Jersey Antitrust Act, P.L.1970, c.73; the Antitrust Act's enforcement provisions (sections 6-17) apply to violations.
rules.quoted_span: any person to perform a coordinating function.

rules.title: Residential rental application fee cap (P.L. 2025, c.405)
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not require an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property that exceeds $50. Violators face civil penalties and must refund the amount wrongfully charged to the applicant.
rules.key_value: $50 maximum, adjusted annually for CPI increases (NY-Northern NJ-Long Island CPI-U)
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property leased or subleased for dwelling purposes; applies to landlords and their agents.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in a one-family or two-family dwelling offered for rent; New Jersey Real Estate Commission licensees, unless the licensee is the landlord of the property.
rules.interaction: State-wide cap with no stated preemption of local rules; local ordinances are not addressed in this document.
rules.quoted_span:

rules.title: NJ Security Deposit Limitation (N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2)
rules.requirement: An owner or lessee may not require a security deposit greater than 1.5 times one month's rent for dwelling property. Any additional security collected annually may not exceed 10 percent of the current security deposit.
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent; annual additional security max 10% of current deposit
rules.coverage_conditions: Real property used for dwelling purposes; applies to owners and lessees collecting security from a tenant.
rules.interaction: State-wide cap; the text does not address local ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: An owner or lessee may not require more than a sum equal to 1 1/2 times 1 month's rental according to the terms of contract, lease, or agreement as a security for the use or rental of real property used for dwelling purposes.
rules.conflict_note: Secondary source (secondary (law firm / news / mirror)); confirm against the official text.

rules.title: S.F. Rent Ordinance Section 37.10C - Prohibition on Algorithmic Rent-Setting Devices
rules.requirement: Prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices (software that analyzes nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rents for vacant units) to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units. Tenants or the City Attorney may bring a civil action for violations.
rules.key_value: Ban on sale or use of algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential units in San Francisco; 'algorithmic device' means a device such as a software program that uses algorithms to analyze nonpublic competitor rental data for the purposes of providing a landlord recommendations on what rent to charge for a vacant unit.
rules.quoted_span: The law prohibits the sale or use of such algorithmic devices and allows a tenant or the City Attorney to bring a civil action if they believe an entity is in violation of the law.

rules.title: San Francisco Ellis Act eviction relocation payments (Rent Ordinance 37.9A)
rules.requirement: Landlords evicting under the Ellis Act must pay relocation amounts. For notices served 3/01/26 - 2/28/27, the amount is $11,110.05 per tenant, up to $33,330.13 per unit, plus $7,443.90 for each elderly (62+) or disabled tenant.
rules.key_value: $11,110.05 per tenant; max $33,330.13 per unit; plus $7,443.90 per elderly (62+) or disabled tenant
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies by date of service of the notice of termination of tenancy (3/01/26 – 2/28/27); elderly means 62 years or older.

rules.title: San Francisco relocation payments for no-fault evictions (Rent Ordinance 37.9C)
rules.requirement: Landlords evicting for owner/relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal from housing use, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation must pay relocation amounts to tenants. For notices served 3/01/26 - 2/28/27, the amount is $8,245.00 per tenant, up to $24,733.00 per unit, plus $5,497.00 for each elderly (60+) or disabled tenant or household with minor child(ren).
rules.key_value: $8,245.00 per tenant; max $24,733.00 per unit; plus $5,497.00 per elderly/disabled tenant or household with minor child(ren)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies by date of service of the notice of termination of tenancy (3/01/26 – 2/28/27); elderly means 60 years or older.
rules.exemptions: Temporary capital improvement evictions for less than 20 days are governed by Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9 instead of Rent Ordinance § 37.9C ($446.00/day plus actual moving expenses for notices 3/01/26 – 2/28/27).
rules.interaction: Short-term temporary displacement (under 20 days) is governed by state Civil Code § 1947.9, not the local ordinance.

rules.title: San Francisco annual allowable rent increase (2026-27)
rules.requirement: For rent-controlled tenancies, the annual rent increase a landlord may impose for the March 1, 2026 - February 28, 2027 period is limited to 1.6%.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance; coverage rules are not stated in this document.
rules.interaction: Local rent control under the Rent Ordinance; the state Tenant Protection Act cap does not apply where stricter local rent control exists. The document does not discuss this.
rules.quoted_span: 1.6% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027

rules.title: San Francisco security deposit interest rate (2026-27)
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay tenants interest on security deposits at the Rent Board's annual rate, which is 4.2% for March 1, 2026 - February 28, 2027.
rules.coverage_conditions: Not specified in this document.
rules.quoted_span: 4.2% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027
